**Method 1**

When we multiply a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always the sum of squares of the real part and the imaginary part.

For the given complex number $z=4+9\text{i},$ the real part is $\text{Re}(z)=4,$ and the imaginary part is $\text{Im}(z)=9,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(\text{Re}(z))^{2}+(\text{Im}(z))^{2} \\  & ={4}^{2}+{9}^{2} \\  & =16+81 \\  & =97.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of multiplying the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=4+9\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=4-9\text{i}.$

Multiplying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(4+9\text{i})(4-9\text{i}) \\  & ={4}^{2}+(4)(-9)\text{i}+(4)(9)\text{i}-{\text{i}}^{2}(9)^{2} \\  & =16-36\text{i}+36\text{i}-(-1)(81) \\  & =16+81 \\  & =97.\end{aligned}
$$
